sentence: This project brings together researchers at seven institutions to find ways to prevent, diagnose and treat cancer.
This project studies how nutrition and metabolism affect health and chronic diseases such as diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disorders.
This project uses computers and experiments to find genetic interactions in cancer cells and how their networks are rewired.
This project studies the mechanisms that control how erythroid cells finish maturing and go through enucleation.
This project studies how a glycoprotein called Reelin takes part in cocaine-dependent signaling in medium spiny neurons.
This project studies small molecular changes in DNA and RNA bases and builds methods to sequence genomes that detect rare base modifications.
This project studies heart disease in children and young adults, including congenital and acquired heart disease, together with other clinical centers.
This project tests whether mitochondria that transfer from cell to cell can supply energy and help recovery after stroke.
This project collects MRI and other neuroimaging from participants in studies of cognitive aging and dementia and shares the processed imaging data with collaborators.
This project builds a method that uses optogenetic stimulation to give precise, place-by-place instructions to developing stem cells.
This project provides imaging methods, including confocal microscopy and X-ray Computed Tomography, to study tissues, cells and animals.
This project tries to make pigs with human skeletal muscle faster and more efficiently, to treat patients with volumetric muscle loss.
This project builds genomics research through two studies, one on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and one on major depressive disorder.
This project builds tools to watch the whole process of horizontal gene transfer in the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae.
This project combines timely real-world data with predictive analytics to detect changes in opioid use and forecast overdose-related outcomes.
This project studies how defects in protein synthesis change stem and progenitor cells and affect red cell biology in anemia.
This project builds nanoscale mechanical techniques and models to study cells and biomolecules and the forces inside cells.
This project builds a Raman scattering microscope that images without labels at higher resolution and compares it with standard Raman scattering microscopy.
This project studies cancers linked to pathogens such as viruses and bacteria, and how the microbiome influences the development of cancers.
This project studies the link between cholestasis and alcoholic hepatitis in a murine model of alcohol-associated liver disease.
